items.title: Chappell Roan Duets With Caroline Polachek, PinkPantheress, and Lola Young
items.summary:
Chappell Roan closed the second night of her two-night benefit run at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles with a string of guest appearances, joining Caroline Polachek for "Look at Me Now" before bringing out PinkPantheress and Lola Young during her own headline set. The concerts, billed as the Super Graphic Spectacular, marked the first anniversary of Roan's Midwest Princess Project, which supports young people from LGBTQ+ communities.

PinkPantheress performed "Tonight" with Roan, and Lola Young joined for "Picture You," according to Pitchfork. Neither guest had been announced in advance, continuing a pattern set the night before.

Wednesday's installment, Roan's first headline set of the two-night event, featured a surprise appearance by Christina Aguilera. The pairing was the kind of cross-generational booking the benefit's loose, variety-show format allowed for.

Roan has been active around Los Angeles beyond her own shows. Last weekend she turned up at the Kia Forum to sing "Boom Clap" with Charli XCX.

The Midwest Princess Project, now a year into its work, was the stated reason for the Shrine dates, with both nights built around the organization's anniversary rather than a tour cycle.

items.title: Paramount+ Head Of Originals Jane Wiseman Leaving As Streamer & HBO Max Combine Operations Post-Merger Under Casey Bloys
items.summary:
Jane Wiseman is leaving Paramount+, where she spent 14 months as EVP and Head of Originals, as the streamer's programming operation folds into HBO Max's under Casey Bloys. Deadline reported the departure, noting that Wiseman's team will now report to Sarah Aubrey, HBO Max's head of originals.

The exit follows that of Wiseman's former boss, Paramount Chair of Direct-to-Consumer Cindy Holland, who left on the eve of Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. After the merger closed on Oct. 6, Bloys became Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, DTC, at the combined Skydance company, taking oversight of HBO, HBO Max and Paramount+ programming.

Bloys brought his longtime HBO lieutenants with him — drama head Francesca Orsi, comedy head Amy Gravitt and Aubrey — leaving no equivalent slot for Wiseman, a senior development executive in her own right. Per Deadline, Bloys spent a couple of weeks examining the Paramount+ operation and weighed having Wiseman keep all or part of her portfolio, including the Taylor Sheridan and 101 Studios slate, under Aubrey, but that arrangement risked upsetting the parity among his three existing executives.

Wiseman ordered 28 new series across scripted, unscripted and kids and family during her tenure, along with 16 renewals, and handled the content side of BET+'s integration into Paramount+. Her slate included Landman, MobLand, The Madison, Dexter and Dutton Ranch, plus upcoming titles Clueless with Alicia Silverstone, Ascent with Viola Davis and Fear Not with Anne Hathaway. The first two scripted series she ordered — Discretion, with Nicole Kidman and Elle Fanning, and The Best of Us, with Jeremy Strong — are in production.

In an internal memo naming his DTC content leadership team, Bloys credited her work. "Jane, in her partnership with Cindy Holland, has done amazing work at Paramount+," he wrote. "The development slate is incredibly impressive, and Jane has graciously offered to help with the transition. She is an extraordinarily talented executive."

Wiseman came to Paramount+ from Sister, where she ran U.S. television under Holland. Before that she was VP and head of comedy at Netflix, overseeing Ozark, Narcos, Russian Doll, BoJack Horseman and Grace and Frankie, and earlier held posts at Chernin Entertainment, NBC and Fox.

items.title: Ryan Gosling’s Spooky Indie Band Dead Man Bones Announce First New Music In 17 Years
items.summary:
Dead Man's Bones, the band Ryan Gosling formed with musician Zach Shields in 2009, has announced new music for the first time since its debut. The group posted a teaser video to social media saying new material arrives Oct. 27, timed to Halloween.

The original album was a genuine oddity of its moment: a self-titled record cut with the Silverlake Conservatory Children's Choir backing the pair, followed by a short run of shows around Halloween 2009. Gosling was between Lars and the Real Girl and Blue Valentine at the time, and few expected the project to resurface.

ANTI- also posted the teaser, which suggests the label will handle the release as it did the 2009 album, Stereogum noted. Gosling's partner Eva Mendes shared the video on her own Instagram with the caption, "He came through on his promise to me."

Gosling's circumstances have changed considerably since the first record. Project Hail Mary is among the year's biggest pictures, he has a Star Wars film, Starfighter, and a Marvel film, Ghost Rider, lined up, and he reached the pop charts singing "I'm Just Ken" in Barbie.

The revival had been hinted at. Asked about a Dead Man's Bones return while promoting Barbie in 2023, Gosling answered, "Maybe. Never say never?" He discussed the band again with NME during the Project Hail Mary press run earlier this year, and Reddit users spotted his and Mendes' stylist Mark Avery posting about the group on Halloween ahead of the announcement.
